newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate pares falls on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate pares falls on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates reined in earlier falls to close down 20 basis points at 18.80 percent Thursday as dealers took profits, traders said.
"The market welcomed the news from Banco de Mexico, and although some threw paper at the market before the close, the trend was definitely downwards," a trader said.
Banco de Mexico announced new mechanisms to dampen volatility in the foreign exchange markets after the close of trade on Wednesday.
Overnight rates on bank paper fell 70 basis points to 19.70 percent.
Dealers said the new mechanisms to restrain sudden swings in the peso would help fend off speculative attacks on secondary interest rates. "They're seeking to contain
speculation and curb demand for a cheap dollar," another trader said.

"If there should be a surge in interest rates in the run-up to elections, it would not be so sharp now," he added, referring to the posibility of market jitters before mid-term Congressional elections to be held on July 6.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 0.15 of a peso firmer at 7.7625/7.7650 per dollar.
Traders said government spending offset liquidity outflows of in corporate tax payments and from an overplacement of paper carried over from the primary auction.
Banco de Mexico participated by draining 3.214 billion pesos from the market, a sign of the liquidity surplus with which the market has operated for much of the year so far.

Liquidity of 1.119 billion pesos was programmed to return to the market on Friday from prior central bank participation. Nonetheless, traders said liquidity could come under some pressure from demand for cash before the weekend.
